- ⚠⚠ **A MISSING TABLE ERRORS; A *DIFFERENT* TABLE RETURNS DATA — AND WHEN TWO TABLES DIFFER BY A PREFIX, THE ORPHAN SORTS FIRST IN A NAME SEARCH** (F2-300, measured 2026-08-23). `BcmExercise` maps `@Table(name = "exercises")`. I measured **`bcm.bcm_exercises`** by name and drew **four** wrong conclusions from it — *zero CHECK constraints*, *a column default of `PLANNED`*, *`PLANNED` is a seed-only synonym of SCHEDULED*, *2 COMPLETED rows with no execution date*. The real table has **three** CHECKs, including `CK_bcm_exer_status` admitting exactly the four tokens the form offers, a status default of `SCHEDULED` matching the entity, **13 rows (COMPLETED ×12 / SCHEDULED ×1)** and **zero** COMPLETED rows without a date. So there was no four-way disagreement, no synonym problem, and no live data defect. 🔑🔑 **`bcm.bcm_exercises` is a V1-era ORPHAN that no `@Entity` maps** — 14 rows, zero CHECKs, holding a `PLANNED` the real register's CHECK would refuse — while `DashboardService` correctly reads `bcm.exercises`. Third instance of the guessed-identifier landmine after [[F2-297]]'s `ndi.gaps` and [[F2-283]]'s `bcm.business_process`, and much the most expensive, **because the wrong table answered every question plausibly.** Resolve the table from `@Table`, and when a name search returns two candidates differing by a prefix, assume the one you did not expect is the live one until `@Table` says otherwise.
  ⚠ **It cost real residue, and the tell was in the cleanup's own output.** The probe's cleanup matched the wrong table, so its first run left 3 rows in `bcm.exercises`; it reported **"deleted 0" against a register whose count had not moved.** 🔑 **A cleanup reporting zero against an unchanged count is not a clean register — it is a cleanup looking somewhere else.** Re-pointed, it deleted 3 and the register returned to 13, with 0 tagged rows in either database.
  ⚙ **The two hazards actually closed**, both latent and both on one method ([[F2-283]]: say which you have). `completeExercise` owns the pair *(status = COMPLETED, `executedDate` stamped from the clock)*, and the entity-bound create and full-replace PUT wrote both fields independently and unconditionally — so either could produce a **COMPLETED exercise with no execution date**, which is the evidence an ISO 22301 / NCEMA reviewer reads to accept the exercise happened ([[F2-188]]/[[F2-191]]'s shape: the duplicate agrees on the row and differs on the part nothing asserts). And `BcmExercise#status` carried `= "SCHEDULED"`, so a partial PUT **silently reset a COMPLETED exercise** — [[F2-238]]'s reset shape and the **sixth** instance of that family after CrisisEvent / Issue / BcmBiaAssessment, [[F2-297]]'s `BcpPlan` and [[F2-298]]'s `BcmPlan`, and it matters more than the row count suggests because **12 of the 13 live rows are COMPLETED**.
  ⚠⚠ **THE GUARD PLACEMENT NEEDED CORRECTING MID-SLICE, AND THE FIRST VERSION FAILED ON CORRECT USAGE.** With `executedDate` still written unconditionally, a partial edit of a COMPLETED exercise nulled the date and then tripped the new invariant — **a 400 on renaming a completed exercise**, the exact trap [[F2-297]] and [[F2-298]] were about. Both fields are null-guarded now, so *omitted* means *leave alone* (the semantics this codebase's PUTs settled on) and the pair moves together; clearing an execution date is therefore not expressible through the PUT, which is the right answer for the field that evidences the exercise happened. 🔑 **The test asserting the old 400 was rewritten rather than kept — a test written against a contract you are about to change is not evidence, it is the old contract.**
  ⚙ **No migration and no new CHECK**, and the reason is worth keeping: `CK_bcm_exer_status` already constrains the column and already agrees with the form, so there is nothing to narrow. The new invariant — *COMPLETED implies an execution date* — **is** expressible as `NOT (status = 'COMPLETED' AND executed_date IS NULL)` and is deliberately enforced in the service instead, because a service refusal names the field **and** the `/complete` route ([[F2-180]]) where a 547 names neither. The create owns its default as a **default**, not `ServerOwnedState.requireInitial`: recording an exercise run offline — created straight into COMPLETED with its date — is legitimate and the create form offers the full select, so a refusal would break working usage ([[F2-214]]).
  ⚙ **Filed:** the **orphan `bcm.bcm_exercises`** — dead schema to drop or a register somebody meant to keep, both owner decisions, and dropping a table in a customer database is not a side effect of a service fix (⚠ **corrected by [[F2-301]]: that half of the filing was redundant** — `TABLE_DISPOSITION.md` has recorded this table since [[F2-141]] and `BASELINE_NO_CODE_TABLES = 36` counts it, so its disposition was never the open question; the **name hazard** was, and F2-301 holds it); and **`bcm.bia_records.status` as free text** — it genuinely has no CHECK, no machine and no transition route (`createBia` sets no status, `updateBia` copies the caller's unconditionally), but **nothing declares a vocabulary for it anywhere**, so a CHECK would invent a lifecycle nobody designed — V375's `consumer.complaint.subcategory` precedent, and [[F2-183]]'s rule rather than reticence.

- ⚠⚠ **A VOCABULARY DOCUMENTED WITH A CITATION IS THE ONE NOBODY CHECKS, AND MINE NAMED A FIFTH STATE THE MACHINE DOES NOT HAVE** (F2-299, measured 2026-08-23). Executing [[F2-298]]'s filing — *"`bcm.bcm_plans` has zero CHECKs on `status`, cheapest now that the writers were touched"* — and re-deriving the writers first ([[F2-221]]). `BcmPlan#status`'s javadoc read `DRAFT | UNDER_REVIEW | APPROVED | INVOKED | ARCHIVED (see BcmService)` and **`ARCHIVED` appears 0 times in `BcmService`, 0 in its controller, 0 in `BcmPage`**. I wrote that line **one slice earlier** by copying the vocabulary of the *canonical* register, `BcpPlan`, which really does have ARCHIVED / PUBLISHED / SUPERSEDED / CANCELLED — so [[F2-234]]'s two-registers-for-one-concept hazard bit the **documentation** before any code. 🔑🔑 **The citation is what made it credible: *"see BcmService"* invites the reader not to look.** And it was load-bearing — **writing V395's CHECK from that line would have admitted a token no route can produce**, which is worse than [[F2-296]]'s *"a CHECK admitting today's values blesses the synonyms"*, because a token nothing writes makes the vocabulary look like **five**: a later reader counting the CHECK concludes the machine has an archive state, and the one artefact that says otherwise is the code they were told they need not read.
  ⚙ **So the gate DERIVES the vocabulary instead of holding a list.** `BcmPlanStatusVocabularyTest` reads the writers — every `setStatus("LITERAL")` on a local of type `BcmPlan`, plus `INITIAL_PLAN_STATUS` by reflection — and asserts that set equals V395's tokens parsed by `MigrationVocabularies`, **both ways**: a token the CHECK admits and no writer produces is a **blessed unreachable state** (this finding), and a token a writer produces and the CHECK refuses turns a legal transition into a **547** surfacing as a 409 naming no field ([[F2-230]]). 🔑 **A hand-written list could not have caught this, because the hand-written list WAS the defect.**
  ⚠ **Scope such a scan by the RECEIVER's declared type.** `BcmService` also writes `e.setStatus("COMPLETED")` on a `BcmExercise` and copies a caller's status onto a `BiaRecord`, so a bare `setStatus\("([A-Z_]+)"\)` sweep of that file would put **COMPLETED** in the plan's vocabulary and then demand the CHECK admit it — a gate failing on correct code ([[F2-214]]). Pinned against the live file, because that literal is really there and its presence is the whole reason the scoping exists.
  ⚙ **F2-183's sequence, in order for once, and that is why it could not have been done sooner.** [[F2-296]] gave the register an echo-tolerant / change-refusing guard on the entity-bound PUT; [[F2-298]] removed the `= "DRAFT"` initialiser that made that guard fire on every non-DRAFT plan. With those closed all five writers are literals or `requireInitial`, and nothing outside `BcmService` writes the column — checked, not assumed. 🔑 **F2-296's own finding was a filing that CLAIMED this state of affairs before it was true; the difference here is that the claim was re-derived rather than quoted.**
  ⚠⚠ **MEASURE OVER ALL ROWS, BECAUSE `ADD CONSTRAINT` VERIFIES SOFT-DELETED ONES TOO.** **10 rows in each database, of which 2 are soft-deleted** — a live-only count reports 8 and misses them. They happen to be DRAFT so nothing was at risk, but a constraint does not respect `@Where(is_deleted = 0)`, and one out-of-vocabulary archived row would have failed Flyway and blocked every later migration on the deployed server.
  ⚙ **V395's self-checks, and the one that is deliberately skippable.** It THROWs on: a pre-flight scan that **names the offending rows** (a bare *"constraint violated"* sends the reader nowhere, and this file blocks every later migration until resolved); the constraint being missing, disabled **or not trusted** (`is_not_trusted = 1` is what a `WITH NOCHECK` add leaves behind and looks identical to a verified constraint in any listing that only checks the name); all four tokens being accepted; and **`ARCHIVED` being refused**, so a later hand-edit cannot widen the CHECK to match the prose this finding is about ([[F2-197]]). ⚠ The last two probe an existing row in a rolled-back transaction, so **on an empty table they verify nothing** ([[F2-183]]'s no-op branch) — and they are deliberately **not** made to fail there, because a fresh install runs this before any plan exists and requiring rows would be a migration asserting **tenant data** rather than its own writes, the exact check [[F2-260]] had to delete from V383 to avoid blocking the chain. The hermetic gate is what covers the empty case.
  ⚙ **Filed:** `bcm.bcp_plans` is already constrained but with **seven** tokens against this register's four, for what the platform presents as one concept — [[F2-234]]'s owner decision, deliberately untouched, because the point of the ARCHIVED finding is that the two vocabularies genuinely differ rather than that one is wrong; and **`bcm.bia_records` and `bcm.bcm_exercises` have no CHECK either while both take a caller's status through `BcmService`**, so unlike the plan register their writers are **open** and F2-183's rule says the constraint cannot go first — reading those two writers is the next unit of work here.

- ⚠⚠ **A GATE WHOSE PATTERN REQUIRES THE NULL TEST TO BE THE *WHOLE* CONDITION IS A HARD ZERO OVER EVERY CONJUNCTIVE GUARD, AND THAT IS WHY THE SAME INITIALISER RECURRED FIVE TIMES** (F2-298, measured 2026-08-23). Executing [[F2-297]]'s filing — *"looks like a live twin; **measure it, do not assume**"* — and re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]). **REFUTED, the half that mattered most: it is not screen-reachable.** `BcmPage`'s plan form seeds its edit modal through `planToReq`, which copies `status: p.status`, and `FormModal` submits its whole seeded state, so the screen **echoes** the stored status and F2-296 made this route tolerate an echo — the same reason [[F2-292]]'s disclosure register survived. 🔑 **Recording the refutation is the result** ([[F2-283]]), and it is what makes this a **latent-hazard closure rather than a defect discovery** — say which you have. **CONFIRMED:** `BcmPlan#status` carried `= "DRAFT"`, `PUT /api/v1/bcm/legacy-plans/{id}` binds the entity, so a body omitting `status` deserialised to "DRAFT" and answered **400 *"A BCM plan's status is not editable here (APPROVED → DRAFT)"*** — naming a transition the caller never asked for. **8 live plans, DRAFT ×5 / APPROVED ×3, zero CHECKs on `status`, 0 non-canonical case**, identical in dev and prod, so **3 of 8 could not take a partial body**.

Only restoring the initialiser and re-running against the real tree found it — it then named exactly `BcmService#updatePlan :: BcmPlan#status`. 🔑 **A positive control written against the shape you imagine certifies nothing** ([[F2-208]]), and the tell was that the control did not fire, not that anything looked wrong. The bare-call form **and** the two-line guard wrap are must-match cases now, because that is what the tree actually contains.

  ⚙ **Filed:** `bcm.bcm_plans` still has **zero CHECKs** on `status` — cheaper now that this slice touched the writers, but the vocabulary lives only in `BcmService` and [[F2-183]]'s rule is one commit for the constraint and its writers; the **full-replace PUT** itself, which writes five fields unconditionally ([[F2-213]]'s structural root, already carried in `FullReplaceUpdateContractTest.DERIVED_IGNORED_FIELDS`); and **two plan registers for one concept** (`bcm_plans` legacy, `bcp_plans` canonical), unchanged from [[F2-234]] and now with a fifth shared defect between them.

- ⚠⚠ **A CENSUS THAT NAMES ITS MEMBERS AND GIVES THEM NO VERDICTS IS A LIST NOBODY READS — AND FOUR OF THESE SEVEN WERE COPIES OF THE RULE THE SLICE THAT FILED THEM HAD JUST SHARED** (F2-297, measured 2026-08-23). Executing [[F2-296]]'s filed 7-site census and re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]): the gate asserts a COUNT and prints nothing, so the sites came from a scan mirroring its detector, which **agreed with it at 7** — and reading each **with its enclosing method** split them three ways that a count could not rank. **Four were hand-rolled copies of the rule F2-296 had just shared**, byte for byte: `if (patch.getStatus() != null && !patch.getStatus().equals(existing.getStatus())) throw "Use transition() to change status"` in `BcpPlanService`, `CrisisEventService`, `IssueService` and `BcmBiaAssessmentService`. The **rule** was right and three things about the copy were not — a bare `equals` against a case-insensitively collated column ([[F2-179]]), a message naming a **Java method a caller cannot call** instead of the route ([[F2-210]], and `BcmBiaAssessmentService`'s said `"status"` where its request carries `approvalStatus`, the exact defect F2-296 found *inside the primitive*), and on `BcpPlanService` an initialised entity field.

[[F2-215]]'s two-of-N at the widest range yet: **the remedy was applied three times, in one module, and the fourth site kept the defect while every artefact around it looked finished.** The create already owned the default through `requireInitial`, so the initialiser was pure residue on create and a refusal on update.
  ⚠⚠ **TWO OF THE SEVEN ARE CORRECT AND MUST NEVER BE CONVERTED, AND THE SAME BARE `equals` INSIDE THEM FAILS IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION.** `CmaDisclosureService#update` and `TcfdItemService#update` legitimately accept `disclosureStatus` ([[F2-231]] established why) and route a *change* through `markReviewed`. A case-variant echo read as a **change**, so it would stamp a CMA Article 92 / IFRS S2 review that never happened and write a `TRANSITION` audit row for a move that never occurred. 🔑 **The four refusal sites fail toward a false 400 — annoying and safe; these two MANUFACTURE A GOVERNANCE RECORD.** One line each (`ServerOwnedState.sameState`, public for exactly this: **the comparison is shared, the refusal is not**). ⚠ Latent everywhere — **0 non-canonical values on all seven columns in both databases** — so what made every one of them harmless was the data and not the code ([[F2-182]]).
  ⚠⚠ **BOTH OF MY FIRST TWO READINGS OF THE LAST MEMBER WERE WRONG.** `NdiGapService#updateGap` writes the caller's status unconditionally and then publishes a `TRANSITION` audit row. I called it *"a PUT that is a reverse edge past whatever the transition route enforces"* — **refuted: that service has no `transition()` and no state machine at all**, so it is [[F2-221]]'s shape, not F2-296's. I then measured `ndi.gaps` and got **TABLE ABSENT in both databases**, which reads exactly like *the register does not exist* — **my own guessed table name**, since the entity says `@Table(name = "gap")`. Resolved properly: **18 rows in both databases, a CHECK on `status` present, 0 non-canonical case, only `OPEN`×9 / `IN_PROGRESS`×9.** So the arbitrary-string harm is **absent** and what remains is whether that vocabulary permits a **jump** past the service's three derivations — the direction a CHECK cannot see. Filed unread, with the ceiling **7 → 1** so it cannot be lost.
  ⚠⚠ **THE TEST THAT COULD HAVE CAUGHT THE LIVE HALF BUILT THE EXACT TRIGGERING PAYLOAD AND PASSED.** `BcpPlanServiceTest.update_cannotEditApprovedPlan` constructs `new BcpPlan()` with only a title — precisely the partial patch that tripped it — and passes because `isLocked()` fires **first** on an APPROVED plan. The broken case is a plan that is neither locked nor in the initial state, and no fixture reached it. [[F2-293]]'s shape with a new mechanism: **an earlier guard masking the one under test, in a fixture that otherwise looks like exactly the right coverage.**
  ⚠⚠ **AND THE STALE CLAIM WAS IN THE FRONTEND, WHERE NO CODE-SCOPED GATE CAN SEE IT.** `CrisisRoomPage.tsx` stated the PATCH body *"must echo the current status because the endpoint binds a JPA entity whose status field defaults to `DETECTED`"* — false since F2-238 removed that initialiser, and exactly the kind of false claim that propagates, because **it tells the next reader to keep a workaround forever** ([[F2-184]] in the place written to be read, [[F2-205]]). Corrected rather than deleted: the echo is harmless and only the *reason* was wrong. 🔑 **It is also the artefact that revealed the whole finding** — a comment in a frontend page named a BCM service's defect precisely, and nothing connected the two.
  ⚠⚠ **A KILL PREDICATE WRITTEN AS AN `-or` WITH ONE UNGUARDED BRANCH DOES NOT MIS-REPORT, IT MIS-KILLS.** Matching the dev JVM by its `-Djava.io.tmpdir` argument without also requiring `Name -eq 'java.exe'` matched **every shell whose command line mentioned that path**, including the harness's own wrappers. [[F2-193]]/[[F2-295]]'s detector-matches-its-own-text family, except this one **acted** on the over-match. The prod-port guard held (8090/8091's PID was skipped and stayed alive) and the repo and both databases were untouched. 🔑 **In a compound kill predicate every branch needs the narrowing, not just the one you wrote last** — and keep the prod-port refusal, because it is the clause that made the mistake survivable.
  ⚠⚠ **A MUTATION HARNESS WHOSE WRITE-VERIFICATION ASSERT SITS *BEFORE* ITS `try/finally` LEAVES THE TREE MUTATED, AND MY ASSERT WAS WRONG ANYWAY.** It read `assert anchor not in on_disk`, which is false for any mutation whose replacement deliberately **contains** its own anchor (one parks the real call behind `if (false)`), so it fired on a perfectly good write — and being outside the `try`, the restore never ran ([[F2-217]]'s landmine). 🔑🔑 **Then `git checkout --` on the file discarded the FIX along with the mutation, because nothing was committed yet on the branch.** The rule that follows is structural, not cosmetic: **commit the slice BEFORE running the harness**, so a crashed harness is recoverable by checkout rather than from memory — and check that the file **CHANGED**, never that the anchor is gone.
  ⚠⚠ **AND THE GATE BUILT FOR THIS EXACT DEFECT HAS ITS POPULATION BOUNDED BY THE SHAPE OF THE *CONDITION*.** `NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` exists for `if (req.getX() != null)` over an initialised field, and [[F2-294]] promoted it to an invariant reading *"Keep it empty. There is no correct code for a hard zero here to fail on."* It passed **15/15 both before and after this slice**, because its guard pattern requires a `)` **immediately after `null`** — the null test must be the *whole* condition — and all four bucket-A guards are **conjunctive** (`!= null && !…equals(…)`). 🔑 **So F2-238's member list did not name `BcpPlan` for a structural reason rather than by oversight** — [[F2-198]]'s shape where the narrowing is neither a filename nor an allow-list nor an HTTP verb but **how much of the `if` the null test occupies.** ⚠ Widening it is **not** a free closure and is therefore filed: the conjunctive shape over an initialised field matches **4 sites** (`BcmService#updatePlan`, `ConsentRecordService#grant` ×2, `DetectionRuleService#save`), at least two of them plausibly legitimate create-or-update paths, so it surfaces a population that must be **read** and four manufactured reasons would be [[F2-188]]'s failure mode.
  ⚠⚠ **AND MY MEASURING SCANNER REPRODUCED A BUG THAT GATE'S OWN COMMENT RECORDS FIXING.** It reported a SIMPLE-shape site (`CloudServiceService#update` over `CloudService#status = "ONBOARDING"`) against a gate that is a hard zero for that shape — **the gate was right**: I keyed initialised fields by **simple class name**, so the two `CloudService` entities (`module/cyber`, `module/outsourcing`) collapsed and the outsourcing initialiser was attributed to the cyber service. F2-238's javadoc describes fixing precisely that, by fully-qualified name. 🔑 **Before writing a scanner, read the scanner this repo already has** — and this phantom is why the conjunctive figure is stated as *four sites to read* rather than as four defects.
  ⚙ **Filed:** the last census member unread; ⚠⚠ **`bcm.bcm_plans` as a possible LIVE TWIN** — `BcmPlan#status` is still `= "DRAFT"` (one entity class, so the hit is real), `PUT /api/v1/bcm/legacy-plans/{id}` binds the entity, and F2-296 made that route tolerate an echo and refuse a change, so a body omitting `status` is refused on any plan not already DRAFT. **Whether it is screen-reachable is unmeasured** (`bcmApi.updatePlan` is called with form `values`, and [[F2-293]]'s rule is that this is a **per-call-site** question), and it is a `PUT` not a `PATCH`, where "omitted means default" is the defensible reading [[F2-238]] used as its own slice boundary — **do not assume it is the same defect; measure it**; `bcm.bia_assessments.approval_status` having **zero CHECKs** in both databases (cheaper now that one writer is closed, but its create path needs reading first — [[F2-183]]); **dev and prod disagreeing on two CHECKs** (`bcm.crisis_events.status`, `platform.issues.status` — constrained in dev, not in prod, purely because those constraints sit inside the pending **V345–V394** range: [[F2-255]]'s reading, recorded so nobody files it as a defect); and all four machines declaring themselves as an inline `switch` + `Set.of(...).contains(...)` ([[F2-284]]'s shape), so the legal-target list is **not derivable at runtime** and every one of the four refusals passes `null` for its `allowed` sentence — converting them to a declared `Map<String, Set<String>>` would let each refusal name the moves the machine would actually accept, and must not be smuggled into a slice about something else.

- ⚠⚠ **ONE QUESTION, FOUR MECHANISMS — AND THE ARTEFACT THAT DOCUMENTS TWO OF THEM DESCRIBES THEM IDENTICALLY WITHOUT NOTICING THEY ARE THE SAME RULE** (F2-296, measured 2026-08-23). *May the caller name the lifecycle state?* The CREATE half has had a shared answer since [[F2-218]] (`ServerOwnedState.requireInitial`, 28 call sites); the UPDATE half had **none**, so four registers answered it four ways: `DisclosureService` hand-rolled it comparing through a `normalise` helper ([[F2-292]]), `EthicsCaseService` hand-rolled it in the **same package** with a bare `equals` on `status` *and* `outcome` ([[F2-291]]), `BcmService` hand-rolled it with a bare `equals` ([[F2-234]]), and `compliance.audit_engagements` had **no copy at all** — `apply()` copied the caller's status with **no vocabulary check and no direction check**, past an `advance()` that is explicitly forward-only (`if (to <= from) throw "must advance forward only"`), so the entity-bound `PUT` was the register's only reverse edge. Probed as `compliance`: a CLOSED IIA engagement walked back to PLANNED, and any string ≤40 chars stored on a NOT NULL column with **zero CHECKs**. Same `COMPLIANCE:WRITE` on create/PUT/advance, so no escalation — the object-level machine was the only control and the PUT sat beside it without one ([[F2-219]]).

  first literal already carries the token; `Dataclass` interpolates it **third**
  (`compile("String " + constant + "…hasAnyRole…")`), so its first literal is just `"String "`. A
  first-literal detector therefore finds one twin and misses the other — **1 of 2, measured** —
  reporting a smaller population, which reads exactly like a partial sweep. Concatenate **every**
  literal in the statement. ⚠ Bound the window to the enclosing statement, **not** a paren-balanced
  walk: a Java regex literal contains real `(` and `)` characters, so counting parens over raw
  source miscounts. Overshooting over-reports, which fails loudly — the safe direction.
  ⚠⚠ **AND THE DISCRIMINATOR IS `has` **AND** `Role`, NEVER `Role` ALONE — BECAUSE THIS PLATFORM HAS

  keyed on a token cannot tell one surface from the other, and the surface it would have swallowed
  is the one the register warns is invisible to every guard scan.**
  ⚙ **The primitive is `com.tss.grc.support.GuardExpressions`** — `rolesRecitedBy` /
  `rawAuthoritiesIn` / `hasRoleLeg` / `isPureRoleGuard` / `guardConstant` /
  `rolesRecitedByConstant` / `stripComments`. `hasRoleLeg` exists so a caller that only needs to
  **classify** a guard never has to declare its own regex, which is what makes the hard zero

  ⚠ **A `hasPermission('MODULE','ACTION')` pair extractor is deliberately NOT in it.** Seven test

- ⚠⚠ **THE ATTRIBUTION QUALITY DECREASED AS THE AUTHORITY INCREASED, AND THE TIER WITH NONE WAS

  for one**. F2-256's shape — the server owns WHEN and nobody owns WHO — at the **top** of a chain
  rather than at its edge, on the artefact an ISO 22301 or SAMA business-continuity reviewer reads.
  🔑 **Stage 0 already demonstrated the correct form** (`preparedByUserId` beside
  `preparedByName`) and each approval stage degraded from it, so the shape to look for is not "is
  there an attribution" but **"does it get worse as you climb?"**

  `BOARD_APPROVE_GUARD` repeated the whole sentence anyway, and F2-254's javadoc repeated it again
  eight paragraphs later. 🔑 **A filing that is half true gets quoted whole** — F2-192's rule that a
  claim about a consequence is the least-verified part of a filing, compounded because nobody who
  quoted it opened the service.

  🔑🔑 **So the missing column, the missing bar and the two zero-holder roles are ONE problem, not
  three.** F2-254 wrote that *"the guard lockout and the missing attribution are one problem and
  F2-52 filed them as two"*; there is a third. Enforcing the bar alone yields a correctly-controlled
  feature **nobody can use** — F2-112's shape **inverted**: not a control that cannot fire but one
  that can only ever fire. Converting the guards alone removes the separation. Doing both decides
  who may give a board-level approval, which is a governance decision about a customer's
  organisation and not a side effect of an attribution fix. **Ship the half that breaks nothing,
  and say why the other half is one decision rather than two tasks.**
  ⚠ **The gate has to assert a withdrawal in BOTH directions**: the attribution is stamped **and**
  neither approval method contains a segregation refusal. A one-directional gate would let the bar
  reappear and the feature quietly stop working — which is the failure mode a reader would blame on
  the guards rather than on the bar.
  ⚠⚠ **A RECORDED BLOCKER CAN BE TWO CLAIMS STACKED IN ONE SENTENCE, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM A
  BLOCKER.** F2-254's read *"the four-eyes bar that would make that safe is not buildable today: …
  there is no identity for either tier to compare. Fixing F2-152 is the prerequisite, and choosing
  who holds a financial versus a board approval is an owner decision plus a migration."* That is
  (a) no identity exists — a fact, and fixable — and (b) who may take which approval — a question.
  🔑 **Stating them as one sentence made the whole thing read as owner-gated, which is how it

  input to somebody's next estimate.

  context, and `mvn -o clean package` is deliberately hermetic (no database, no secrets), so the
  build never starts the app either. 🔑 **The only instrument that could see it was launching it,
  and a launch is not part of the build** — under a Maven `BUILD SUCCESS`, per the recorded landmine
  that `BUILD SUCCESS` is not a start signal for `spring-boot:run`. F2-222 filed this shape for
  *entities* and measured it latent (15 of 433 names in two packages); for a bean it is fatal.
  `UniqueBeanNameContractTest` holds it at a hard zero over **744** component-scanned beans, with no
  exemption map — an explicit `@Component("name")` is always available, so there is no correct code
  for it to fail on (F2-214). Prefer the distinguishing NAME over the alias: when two modules each
  resolve their own register, a reader reaching for whichever they found first is the real hazard.
  ⚠⚠ **`io.open(path, "w")` TRUNCATES ON OPEN, so an exception during the write leaves the file at
  ZERO BYTES — and that destroyed the 1.79 MB findings register.** The write raised
  `UnicodeEncodeError` (lone surrogates: `\ud83d\udd11` written as two escapes is two unpaired
  surrogates, not the character), by which point the file was already empty. 🔑 **Every subsequent
  grep then answered "not found", which reads as the anchor having moved rather than as the file
  having been destroyed** — three tool calls went into hunting a phantom rename. It was tracked and
  uncommitted, so `git checkout --` restored it. **Build the content, write a TEMP file, assert the
  round-trip, then `os.replace`.** ⚠ Its sibling in the same session: a patch script whose write
  handle was never closed, so its own verifying `assert` re-read an unflushed file, found nothing and
  passed vacuously. **Use a context manager, and never let a script certify its own write.**
  ⚠⚠ **AN ENTITY-BOUND CREATE HAS NO SETTER FOR A SCAN TO FIND, so "the service does not write X
  from the request" is VACUOUS over it.** My first gate leg asserted exactly that and the pre-fix
  control reported it **SILENT ON MASTER** — Jackson had already bound `vendorId` and `vendorName`
  onto the entity and the service mentioned neither, so there was nothing for `setX(req.…)` to
  match, and the leg would have passed forever over the defect it was written for. 🔑 **On an
  entity-bound endpoint the load-bearing assertion has to be the POSITIVE** — the field must be
  *overwritten from the resolver* — which is the only shape that can see a create doing nothing at
  all. This is why F2-206's introspector exists for the server-owned fields; a business foreign key
  has no such mechanism.

  deriving a second copy from a resolved parent, check the two sides use the same notation**; the
  form's own cap was the tell.

  **39** places — 18 with a query between the two saves, 21 without. ⚠ The mapping is what makes it
  fatal: `BaseEntity.rowVersion` is `@Version @Column(insertable = false, updatable = false)` on a

  ⚙ **Filed as the structural root:** annotating `rowVersion` `@Generated(event = {INSERT, UPDATE})`

  fixture is wrong for three hours of every day (F2-178 correction, caught 2026-08-10 at 00:4x local).
  `CommitteeSeatLinkageTest` set `termEndsAt = LocalDate.now().minusDays(1)` while
  `CommitteeMemberRegistryService`/`CommitteeSeatAuthority` read `LocalDate.now(Clock.system(ZoneId.of("UTC")))`;
  between local midnight and 03:00 the two disagree by a day and a lapsed seat reads as current. It had
  merged **green** the day before. **Inject the clock and pin the date** (`Clock.fixed` on a `TODAY`
  constant that is deliberately *not* today — a fixed date equal to the real one proves nothing about the
  injection). ⚠ A mutation harness scoped to a slice's own tests cannot catch this: the failing class was
  not in its list.
- `seed_real_data.py` batches must start `SET NOCOUNT ON;`.
- Don't "seed" an empty table before checking it's wired (`privacy_lc` is orphaned).
- **The intake substrate is the platform front door, and until F2-172 it filed every submission
  into the submitter's own browser.** Now server-backed end to end: `useIntake()` calls
  `POST/GET/PUT /api/v1/intake`, `SEED_INTAKE`'s 5 fabricated records and the `grc.intake`
  localStorage overlay are deleted, and the client-side `generateReferenceCode()`/`slaDeadline()`
  minters are **deleted rather than moved** — only the server may issue a tracking code or a
  statutory deadline. `lib/intake.ts` no longer touches `localStorage` on **any** path; a signed-in
  failure surfaces as an error and the public portal *says* it is blocked (F2-138) rather than
  issuing a code.
  ⚠ **Four things about this module a reader will otherwise get wrong:**
  **(a) `POST /api/v1/intake` is `isAuthenticated()`, not permission-guarded**, and that is an
  ADR-010 §Sanctioned exception, pinned in `ControllerAuthorizationRatchetTest`'s `SELF_SCOPED`
  floor with `IntakeSubmitGuardTest` holding the expression. It was `INTAKE:WRITE`, measured as
  **3 of 69 roles, all administrators** — so an ordinary employee could not report a security
  event (NCA ECC 6.1), a privacy breach (PDPL Art. 27) or a workplace injury (GOSI 24 h). Do not
  "restore consistency" by converting it. READ and TRIAGE stay permissioned: filing is a duty,
  reading other people's whistleblowing reports and DSRs is a privilege.
  **(b) `submitterIsAnonymous` is a REQUEST, not an instruction.** The server honours it only for
  the kinds whose `IntakeKindRouting` entry sets `allowsAnonymous` (SPEAKUP, BREACH_REPORT,
  VRP_DISCLOSURE) — obeying it unconditionally would let any caller make any submission
  unattributable and defeat the `submitter_user_id` binding through the field that exists to
  protect whistleblowers. Where it IS honoured, **nothing identifying is stored** and
  `submitter_user_id` is NULL by design (V374 self-checks THROW if the column is made NOT NULL).
  **(c) The kind catalogue exists TWICE** — `IntakeKindRouting` (Java, in `intake/service/`) and
  `INTAKE_CATALOG` (`lib/intake.ts`) — pinned field-by-field, in both directions, by
  `IntakeCatalogueParityTest`. The server held **16** of the frontend's **26** for months while its
  javadoc claimed they were mirrored; the ten it rejected included the 24-hour GOSI injury
  notification. Add a kind to both. `titleAr` is part of the pin and is **not** decoration — a
  promoted record's mandatory `title_ar` is composed from it.
  **(d) Promotion creates the register record SERVER-side, and the client cannot name it.**
  `PUT /api/v1/intake/{id}/triage` resolves the **target from the kind's catalogue entry**, calls an
  `intake.spi.RegisterPromotionPort`, and stamps `promoted_to_record_id` **from the row it wrote**,
  in one transaction. The request DTO has no field for either — do not re-add one. (Both halves used
  to be broken at once: `lib/intake.ts` drove the lifecycle in `localStorage`, *and*
  `IntakeService.triage()` took `promotedToRecordId` from the request body and created nothing.)
  ⚠⚠ **A promoted record's status/category words are governed by a `CHECK` the Java side never mentions,
  and three of the thirteen adapters were writing values their columns had never accepted** (F2-180 +
  F2-175): `RiskPromotionAdapter` `IDENTIFIED`, `VendorPromotionAdapter` `ONBOARDING`, and
  `IncidentPromotionAdapter` passing the submitter's own category straight through — so `SECURITY_INCIDENT`
  (**0 of its form's 4 categories legal**), `WORKPLACE_INJURY` and `CONSUMER_COMPLAINT_RESPONSE` could
  never promote, and only `VRP_DISCLOSURE` — which has no category field — ever worked. All three words
  were right about what the state *means*. 🔑 **Being right about what a state means is not evidence about
  what the column stores it in.** Now pinned by `PromotionVocabularyTest`: 13 adapters → 13 target tables →
  18 CHECK vocabularies, read from the **migrations** so `mvn package` stays hermetic, with every
  constrained column either bound to a named constant or listed in `unwritten` with a reason. All 13 are
  live-probed (50/50) as of 2026-08-11.
  ⚠ **The reason it was three and not eight is one accessor**: `IntakePromotionContext#severityOrMedium()`
  clamps to the four bands all five severity-ish columns declare. **A closed column needs a closed writer** —
  add a clamp, do not trust the caller, and do not widen the CHECK to admit whatever the caller sent.
  ⚠ **Error 547 is BOTH `FOREIGN KEY` and `CHECK`**, and `GlobalExceptionHandler` reported every one as a
  reference problem — costing three investigations, including one on `risk.risks`, a table with no foreign
  keys at all. It now answers `conflictKind: VALUE_NOT_ALLOWED` and names the column (the 547 CHECK message
  carries the column but not the value, so SEC-CFG-001 holds). If you see the old wording, you are on an
  old jar. 🔑 **A wrong-but-specific diagnostic does not slow the reader down, it sends them somewhere.**
  ⚠ **The 13 adapters live in the module that OWNS the record** (`privacy/intake/`, `risk/intake/`…),
  never in `module/intake`: ADR-018 homes intake in **Base**, and twelve of the fourteen targets are
  sold SKUs. `IntakePromotionContractTest` fails the build if `module/intake` imports a peer. The
  `CHANGE` adapter is the exception and sits in `change_adapters`, because ADR-012 forbids
  `module/change_mgmt` importing a peer — that guard refused the obvious placement and was right to.
  ⚠ Promotion also requires the **target module's own write permission** on top of `INTAKE:TRIAGE`,
  and guessing it from the target name is the trap: the ethics register and the whole policy module
  are guarded by **`COMPLIANCE:WRITE`**, not `ETHICS:WRITE` — and `ETHICS` *does* exist in the
  catalogue, so the obvious guess compiles and 403s.
  ⚠ **Six `CONTROL_TEST` kinds have no register and now 409 by design** (F2-176). A promotion that
  cannot create the record must refuse, not flip the status and write nothing.
  ⚠ **There is exactly ONE writer to `intake.intake_records`, and that is now enforced** (F2-175).
  `MlModelDriftService` used to build the entity itself and call `intakeRepo.save()`, so none of the above
  governed the CRITICAL-drift path: hard-coded assignee, its own `ISS-…` code minter, its own
  `plusDays(14)`, no history events, and hand-concatenated JSON whose `esc()` covered only
  `\`/`"`/`\n`/`\r` — **so a model title containing a TAB produced a record that could never be promoted**,
  failing as *"unreadable payload"* from `intake` while the fault sat in `ai/governance`.
  **A peer module files a submission through `intake.spi.SystemIntakePort`** (the inbound counterpart to
  `RegisterPromotionPort`), which takes a `Map` payload the mapper serialises — so promotability is
  structural, not lucky. `IntakeSingleWriterInvariantTest` pins three hard zeros/ones: `new IntakeRecord(`
  appears **once** in main sources, `IntakeRecordRepository` has **one** user, and **no peer imports
  anything of `module/intake` but its `spi`**. ⚠ Invariants, not ratchets — the population is one, so a
  raisable count would make a tolerated writer look reviewed.
  🔑 Three reusable lessons from it: **(a)** the register's own filing called the bypass *"currently
  benign"* when the supportable claim was *"unexercised"* — 26 seeded drift rows, `triggered_issue_id`
  NULL on all of them, so the path had **never run**; **(b)** two of the filing's three architectural
  claims were false (`ai → intake` is SKU → Base, the *legal* direction, and `ModuleGraphRatchetTest`'s
  `KERNEL_ISH` is only `{platform, integrations, dashboard}` so it could not fire) — **read the guard
  before believing a finding's claim about it**; **(c)** the existing test asserted the defect as
  correct (`startsWith("ISS-")`, `isEqualTo("SUBMITTED")`), the second instance after F2-159 —
  **a test written by reading the implementation can only agree with it.**
  ⚠⚠ And the honest half: the catalogued assignee `RISK_OFFICER` **did not exist in `iam.roles`** while
  the hard-coded `RISK_MANAGER` did. It was still the right change — one catalogue, consulted — but the
  value it consulted was wrong: **10 of 14 catalogue codes matched no role**, carrying **22 of 26 kinds**.
  🔑 **The hard-code F2-175 deleted was right about the name and wrong about the mechanism.**
  ⚠⚠ **`defaultAssignee` is a ROLE NAME from `iam.roles`, not a free-text stakeholder label** (F2-174,
  closed 2026-08-11). All 14 codes had a real counterpart already seated, so the ten that named nothing
  (`CISO_OFFICE`, `ETHICS_CTE`, `CSIRT`, `RISK_OFFICER`, `COMPLIANCE_LEAD`, `POLICY_OFFICER`, `TPRM_LEAD`,
  `BCM_LEAD`, `AUDIT_LEAD`, `CAB`) were renamed, and `IntakeAssigneeRoleResolutionTest` holds a **hard
  zero** against the one pinned catalogue (`RoleGuardConversionRatchetTest.ROLE_CATALOGUE` — its **third
  reader, not a third copy**). Do **not** read it as "the assignee now works": only **4 of 11** names have
  an active holder in dev or prod, nothing resolves the column (it renders as a label in the ack text and
  the audit note), and `assigned_to` **collates differently** from `iam.roles.role_name`
  (`Latin1_General_100_CI_AS_SC_UTF8` vs `SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS`) — so a resolver's bare join raises
  *"Cannot resolve the collation conflict"* 468/8180 and must `COLLATE` explicitly.
  ⚠ **Both fixes the filing proposed were non-viable, and only measurement showed it**: failing closed at
  runtime would refuse the 24-hour GOSI injury notification over a label (contradicting the ADR-010
  exception above), `0 of 14` codes matched any committee so the seat machinery was not reusable, and
  `workflow.recipient_list_members` is **empty in both databases**. 🔑 **A filing's candidate fixes are
  the least-verified thing in it after its recommendations.** ⚠ And its urgency was false:
  `intake.intake_records` held **0 rows in dev and prod**, so the field had never once been written.
